architecture: v3 (architecture 3, re-root at wave 1: older-dog renewal increases and the owners who leave)
slot_note: wave-1 re-root of task128 (v1 solved in-house, v2 spent at the re-root): a new world and decision in the same objective
niche: a Swedish pet insurer choosing which of its older-dog breed-group books take their indicated 2027 renewal increase, sized by what the chosen increases add to the result of the renewed policy year once the owners who leave are counted at their own dogs' cost
stakeholder_role: product owner for dog insurance at a Swedish pet insurer, who sets the 2027 renewal increase on the older-dog book

spine.entity: one dog's policy year (inception or renewal to the next anniversary)
spine.source: synthetic (a fictional Swedish pet insurer's policy administration extract)

world.org_type: pet insurer writing veterinary-care and life cover for dogs and cats

driver: The decisive quantity is what a price rise adds once the members it sheds are priced at their own expected cost, because members tied to the cover by an ongoing condition cannot move to another provider while the members cheapest to serve leave most readily, so the book that stays costs more per member than the book did; pricing the extra leavers at the book's average cost, or ignoring them, makes the largest rise look best when a smaller one adds most.
driver_concrete: Owners of older dogs with no ongoing condition lapse more for every point of renewal increase and cost a fraction of their book's average, while dogs under treatment almost all renew; in the books where the leavers are many and cheap the indicated increase loses more on the dogs that leave than it gains on the dogs that stay, so only some of the five breed-group books should take theirs.
stump: A competent solver applies each book's indicated increase to its renewing premium, measures from the past renewals how many more owners lapse per point of increase in each book, and counts the extra leavers at the book's average claims cost, which keeps all five books; the step that lands it there is pricing the leavers at the book's average cost, when the owners who leave after an increase are those whose dogs have no ongoing condition and cost a fraction of the average while dogs under treatment stay, so two books' increases take money off the result and only the other three add.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who links each dog's policy years across re-issued policy numbers by microchip, separates lapses from deaths and transfers, measures the lapse response to every past renewal increase and applies the 2027 options exactly as the tariff states still prices the extra leavers at the book's average cost (or at the cost of dogs of the same age and breed) and sets the largest increase, because only rebuilding which dogs carry an ongoing condition from their claims history shows that the leavers are the cheap dogs and the stayers the costly ones.
domain_test: Pricing actuarial work decides the call: the result a renewal rate change buys depends on the renewal (retention) response and on anti-selection, the claims cost of the policyholders who leave against those who stay, which pet insurance makes acute because a pre-existing condition is excluded by any new insurer; with another field's nouns there is no renewal, no claims cost and no exclusion that ties a member to the cover, so the task does not survive the swap.
layer1: policy numbers re-issued when a policy is reinstated or the owner changes, the dog's microchip number the stable key, written with and without spaces and the country prefix
lapses, deaths, transfers to a new owner and cancellations for non-payment in one renewal-outcome field set by different systems
claims keyed to the policy number in force at treatment, with re-opened and duplicated claims from the clinic direct-settlement feed
diagnosis codes from two coding versions after a 2023 coding change
premiums with and without the 2024 insurance-premium tax change, monthly instalment plans against annual payment
the tariff change log by segment and effective date, a renewal taking the change in force at its anniversary

lineage.architecture: v1 (harden loop 0): whole-host rebuild valuation as the decisive rung, one colocated ticket spending the month's drains
lineage.fate: solved by the in-house plain solver in round 1 (2026-10-10); kept as the stop rung of loop 1
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what one use of the binding resource removes, which is everything on the member that the current baseline fixes rather than the single item the request names, because each use rebuilds the member from that baseline; a ledger that credits each request with its own item reproduces every closed period, so per-item valuation spends the scarce uses on the members with the richest single item instead of the members carrying the most in total, and the constrained candidates need far fewer requests for far more removal than the per-item reading allows.

lineage.architecture: v2 (harden loop 1): the ticket's reach, a ticket one change request for one window
lineage.fate: spent at the wave-1 re-root (2026-10-12): its decisive step reads a filed rule (rule application, banned as the decisive step), the card's strategy repeats task127's, and the world (IT patch remediation) has no client-domain task type serving Opportunity Sizing
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many requests it takes to spend a binding resource whose budget is stated for the whole period, because each request draws only on the capacity of the one interval it is booked into; a plan that values every use correctly but files one request against the period's whole budget reaches one interval's share, so the constrained candidates need one request per interval and the unconstrained candidates give up that many places under the cap.

differentiation.task501: task501 sizes a standby facility from funds' drawdown pace against investment-period deadlines; task128 v3 prices the policyholders a renewal increase sheds at their own dogs' claims cost, and the shed members are the cheap ones because the costly ones cannot move.

notes: Re-root of task128 to architecture 3, drawn 2026-10-12, after v1 (solved in round 1) and v2 (spent at the wave-1 re-root: its decisive step read a filed rule, and IT patch remediation has no client-domain task type serving Opportunity Sizing). Opportunity Sizing: the pool is the renewing older-dog premium, realised through the renewal response and the leavers' own claims cost. Anti-selection is also the driving force of seed DS27 (task373, motor re-rating by sales channel, unbuilt); this build's mechanism is captivity by a condition no other insurer covers, rebuilt from claims history, on a dial rather than an allocation.
